findings.summary: The finalizer accepts the retired pi_cold_agent_boundary@3 generation for revision-6 records, so the final-result proof does not mechanically enforce boundary generation 4 (exact readable/writable /dev/null, no other device or alias exception).
findings.evidence: Reproduced on the offline fixture: I built a valid revision-6 author subject/checker pair, then downgraded only the checker boundary.json from nomos.pi_cold_agent_boundary@4 to nomos.pi_cold_agent_boundary@3 (rename deviceFilesystemExact to the old deviceFilesystemEmpty check, drop deviceNullReadable/deviceNullWritable, set legacy systemPromptSha256 2cec3a... and finalSystemPromptSha256 a78cae...), refreshed all bound digests via the shipped helpers, and gate-k-eval-finalize.sh succeeded: `GATE_K_RUN_FINALIZED verdict=pass` with result.json `.records.checker.dimensions.operational_compliance.verdict == "pass"`. The finalizer jq at line 490-491 allows `.schema == "nomos.pi_cold_agent_boundary@3"` for any runtimeIdentity-bearing record, and line 522-526 accepts the old check allowlist containing only `deviceFilesystemEmpty`; there is no rule forcing non-legacy revision-6 records to be @4. COLD_AGENT_PROTOCOL.md revision 6 prescribes boundary schema nomos.pi_cold_agent_boundary@4 and COLD_AGENT_PROTOCOL's /dev/null exactness guarantee (deviceFilesystemExact/deviceNullReadable/deviceNullWritable) was closed in the e2e0cfb/66c96f4 repair, so @3 is exactly the earlier falsified guarantee ('deviceFilesystemEmpty'). pi-cold-agent-task.sh does require @4 at generation time, but the finalizer is the final assembly gate and it does not fail closed on a stale @3 boundary.

No operator message, coaching, retry, repair, or follow-up occurred during this review; only the pinned read/bash tooling was used and the checkout was left clean (zero untracked files after cleanup of the temporary cbfa3f7 worktree and scratch dirs).
